target_customer: Restaurants, cafes, hotels and wet markets in Indonesia buying fruit and vegetables, plus the farmers who supply them
problem: Indonesia's multi-layer middleman food supply chain makes prices volatile, cutting farmer income and raising restaurants' raw material costs.
business_model: B2B food distribution with margin on produce, ordering app, ERP and farmer app, later financing products and a seasoning consumer brand
product_category: B2B agritech and fresh produce supply chain

founders.name: David Setyadi Gunawan
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has been an active retail trader in Indonesian stocks and crypto since 2014. e27 names him founder and CEO. Education not found.

founders.name: Ramavito Mountanio
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked in capital markets at Manulife Asset Management Indonesia and later became CFO of SWAP Energy. e27 spells the surname Mountaino.

founders.name: Febrianto Gamal
founders.background_notes: Listed as COO by e27 and as a founder on the YC page. No background given.

competitors.name: Sayurbox
competitors.what: Indonesian online fresh produce marketplace that later also sold B2B, adjacent to Eden Farm
competitors.funding_then: Tokopedia reported investment, per a link on the DealStreetAsia page

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering app, ERP and farmer app are standard software. The hard part was operations: logistics, cold chain and farmer supply, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Supplier relationships and delivery density help, but produce distribution has thin margins and several startups chased the same buyers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Peers competed rather than bought. DealStreetAsia reported acquisition talks with Sayurbox, initiated by investors, after layoffs, outcome not confirmed.

market_need_then: Indonesia had a multi-layer middleman supply chain with volatile prices, which the YC pitch cites as the problem hurting farmers and restaurants.

branding.domain_note: Uses edenfarm.id, the Indonesian country domain, not a .com (source: company URL).
branding.brand_signature: Launched a consumer seasoning brand called TuangTuang in September 2023 per press
branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found of brand community; press covers funding and layoffs.

brand_strength.rationale: A B2B supplier brand known in trade press, with no consumer visibility until the seasoning brand and no sourced evidence of brand pull.

pivots.from: Fresh produce distribution to restaurants and markets across regions
pivots.to: Focus on TuangTuang seasoning brand and Greater Jakarta operations
pivots.why: Press says demand fell for vegetable distribution outside Jabodetabek and the company shut distribution there.

outcome_analysis: Eden Farm raised a $1.7M seed in September 2019, a $19M Series A in late 2021 and about $13.5M in early 2023, then confirmed a mass layoff of about 300 people in September 2023 and shut regional distribution as it pivoted toward a seasoning brand. Further cuts and merger talks with Sayurbox were reported. Thin food distribution margins, scaling beyond Jakarta and the funding downturn explain the contraction, though the company is still listed active.
notes: Company website returned 503. The 2023 round: DealStreetAsia calls it pre-Series B at $13.5M, startupintros says Series B at $14M and Seedtable $13.02M, so recorded as other with the DealStreetAsia amount. Funding from the headline of the Series A is $19M; e27 article undated, dated by outlet headline as 2021-11-08 matching the YC page news item. Total raised per search summaries is $33.7M to $34.5M, roughly matching recorded rounds. Sayurbox is listed as an adjacent player only because the 2019 source links to it, it is not named as a competitor there. Layoff size of 300 comes from search summaries of The Bridge Club and DealStreetAsia, the DealStreetAsia page is paywalled. Merger talks with Sayurbox are reported by sources, outcome not confirmed. A source dated 2023-02 mentions a further layoff on Feb 21 (year unconfirmed).
